title: The loonie's 19-month low

lines: US cents — that's about all one Canadian dollar now buys, as the loonie hits a 19-month low.
The Canadian dollar slid to around 1.43 per US dollar this week — its weakest since April 2025.
A loonie now buys roughly 69-70 US cents. (Reuters, The Globe and Mail, Nov 2026)
The push came from the US side: hotter US jobs and inflation data and hawkish Fed comments.
That widened the gap between US and Canadian interest rates and pulled money into the greenback.
A weaker loonie makes anything priced in US dollars cost Canadians more.
Winter produce, fuel, US online orders and trips south of the border all get pricier.
A stock crash grabs the headlines, but a 19-month-low loonie is the quieter tax — it touches almost everything a Canadian household buys.
Have you felt the weak loonie at the checkout or the border?

source_line: Sources: Reuters, The Globe and Mail, FXStreet - Nov 20, 2026
caption:
One Canadian dollar now buys only about 70 US cents - and if you live in Canada, that quietly makes a lot of your spending more expensive.

The loonie slid to around 1.43 per US dollar this week, its weakest level since April 2025 - a 19-month low (Reuters, The Globe and Mail, Nov 2026). The push came from the US side: hotter US jobs and inflation data plus hawkish Fed comments widened the gap between US and Canadian interest rates and pulled money into the greenback. Canadian retail sales rose 0.8% in September, released today, giving the currency only a brief pause.

A weaker loonie doesn't show up on a stock ticker - it shows up at the till. Anything priced in US dollars (winter produce, fuel, US online orders, cross-border shopping and trips south) costs Canadians more.

My take: a market crash grabs the headlines, but a 19-month-low loonie is the slower, quieter tax - it touches almost everything a Canadian household buys.
